newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia votes against some new taxes in 1997.
newsitem.headline: Russia votes against some new taxes in 1997.

text.p: A conciliation commission of parliament and government voted on Thursday against some new government tax proposals, cutting 1997 draft budget revenues by 35-37 trillion roubles from the planned 432.8 trillion roubles.
The commission was set up after the State Duma lower house rejected the draft 1997 budget, criticising it for over-optimistic revenue plans and low social spending.

"The Duma and the Federation Council (upper house) voted against lifting of concessions on the taxation of profit spent for investment, against imposing value-added tax on invoices and against rising excises for petrol to 35 percent from the current 20 percent," Duma budget committee chairman Mikhail Zadornov, a member of the commission, told reporters.
Duma representatives proposed restoring export duties on oil and gas and increasing average import tariffs on all goods to 15.0 percent from a current 13.7 percent.
A ban on export duties was one of the conditions sought by the International Monetary Fund for its $10 billion loan.
When asked how government officials reacted to the duties proposal, Zadornov said that they were not categoric in rejecting the proposal.
He said the commission would discuss the problem on Friday in detail.
"The final decision of the export duties problem will depend on the calculations for replacing them which we shall receive tomorrow," Zadornov said.
He said that the government had lost 13 trillion roubles from abolishing export duties, while excises, which replaced the duties, would bring in only half of the lost revenues.
